item.title: Biff Poggi makes his case to become Maryland’s next head football coach
item.description: Biff Poggi makes his case to become Maryland’s next head football coach originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Former Michigan Wolverines interim coach Biff Poggi threw his name in the mix to be Maryland's next head football coach. Poggi was born in Baltimore and has ties to the area. The 66-year-old Big Ten Network analyst marveled at the chance to become the Terrapins' next head man in charge. “Yeah, I really would like the job,” Poggi said in a phone interview with the Baltimore Sun . Poggi coached at Gilman and St. Frances Academy in Baltimore. At Gilman, he had a 135-43 record, won 13 conference championships and was the winningest coach in school history. At St. Frances, he helped an underfunded Catholic school become national contenders. Poggi told the Baltimore Sun that he firmly believes Maryland has the talent and resources to win in the Big Ten. “Don’t think you can think, ‘Hey, we’re just going to hire a new coach, and everything’s going to be better,'” Poggi said. “There have been plenty of coaches there that haven’t won.” In Poggi’s three-game stretch as the Wolverines' interim coach, he went 2-1 and lost 41-27 to Texas in the Citrus Bowl. But this was during his third tenure at Michigan. He originally joined Michigan with Harbaugh in 2016 as an analyst before returning in 2021 and 2022 as associate head coach. During his second tenure, the Wolverines went 25-3 and made appearances in the College Football Playoffs. Despite his success in Michigan, his stint at Charlotte was nothing like it. Poggi spent two seasons as head coach in Charlotte, posting a 6-16 record before returning to Michigan in 2025. Poggi laid out his plan to rebuild, including hiring like-minded coaches with similar goals and attacking the transfer portal aggressively. He also mentioned how Maryland struggles to attract renowned assistant coaches and took a shot at their "pretty weak" coaching staff. Poggs estimates Maryland needs $25 million to $28 million annually in player compensation to build a competitive roster, combining institutional revenue sharing with corporate sponsorships. “If Indiana can win, we can win." Although Poggi has not spoken to Maryland's athletic director, Jim Smith, he believes he has the resources and knowledge of the area to win, and his resume speaks for itself. “If I was named the Maryland coach, I would have 50 calls that day from kids and their agents." Will Maryland come calling? We will see what happens next. item.title: Buccaneers get bad news with Emeka Egbuka injury update for Baker Mayfield's return
item.description: Buccaneers get bad news with Emeka Egbuka injury update for Baker Mayfield's return originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers is a must-win game. They're facing off against the Carolina Panthers , the NFC South division leader, sitting at 3-2. The Buccaneers, meanwhile, are 1-5 on the year. A Week 7 loss would effectively end their season. So, with so much on the line this week, it's some great news that Baker Mayfield is expected to come back after a multi-game absence due to a thumb injury. But it's not all good news. Unfortunately, as Greg Auman of Fox Sports shared, the Buccaneers' injury report reveals Emeka Egbuka, Mayfield's top target, is going to miss this weekend's matchup. Buccaneers get bad Emeka Egbuka news for Week 7 The injury report for the Buccaneers revealed that Egbuka has a "concussion/knee" injury, and following DNPs on Wednesday and Thursday, he was a limited participant on Friday. But even though his practice status was upgraded by the end of the week, there wasn't enough time for Egbuka to return in full capacity for the Buccaneers. Unfortunately, as the season is seemingly on the line in Week 7, the offense will have to beat a Panthers defense without its top receiver. MORE : Aaron Rodgers blasts Buccaneers' field as 'one of the worst surfaces in the league' Chris Godwin and Ted Hurst will be busy this week, with Tez Johnson and tight end Cade Otton getting into the mix as well. Bucky Irving could be in store for a huge week as well. While there's some optimism about the Buccaneers heading into this game with Mayfield's return, they're losing a key player for this matchup as well, with Egbuka ruled out on Friday. Egbuka's injury should not be a long-term issue, but he's not playing in Week 7, when the Buccaneers really could use him. If Mayfield can pull this off against the Panthers, it would be quite an impressive win for the new $165 million QB. item.title: 'No reply to this day': Amit Mishra reveals shocking cold shoulder from Virat Kohli after 2017 comeback snub
item.description: 'No reply to this day': Amit Mishra reveals shocking cold shoulder from Virat Kohli after 2017 comeback snub originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Amit Mishra claims Virat Kohli never replied after promising him a return once he was fit. Mishra dialled Kohli several times but got no response. His last India appearance came in February 2017, ending a career of 68 internationals. Amit Mishra accuses Virat Kohli of breaking comeback assurance Amit Mishra says he is still waiting for an answer from Virat Kohli, nearly a decade after a comeback that he believed was coming but never arrived. The veteran leg-spinner has spoken about his failed return to the India side, and he claims the then captain promised him another chance but went silent once he had recovered from injury. According to Mishra, the trouble began when he hurt his leg during a T20I against England in Bengaluru. He said that Kohli urged him to focus on his recovery and assured him that he would be back in the team as soon as he was fit. MORE: Women's and Men's T20 World Cup 2028: Dates, host nations, and tournament format explained In an interview with Aakash Chopra, Mishra revealed “I also asked Virat Kohli, I said, ‘Brother, what needs to be done?’ He said, ‘You don’t worry. Get fully fit and comfortable, and you are there [in the team].’” Mishra got in touch with Kohli once his rehabilitation was done, hoping to hear about a return. Kohli, he said, asked him to wait for a week before the captain came back to him. Mishra said: “So he said, ‘I will let you know in a week to ten days.’ Then, brother, one week passed, two weeks passed, three weeks passed; there was absolutely no update from him. I called him… he did not pick up the call. I messaged him, but there was no reply.” MORE: WTC 2027 Final: Qualification scenarios, chances and probabilities BCCI/Sportzpics What Amit Mishra wanted from Virat Kohli: A response and a fair chance to prove fitness A big part of Mishra’s frustration comes from the form he had shown before he was hurt, and from what he saw happening to other players. He asked why those who had suffered worse injuries and spent longer away from the game were brought back after regaining fitness, while he never got a clear answer. Mishra said: “When players who got more severely injured than you, and were injured for much longer, made their comebacks… yet, I have never received any answer to this day.” He said that once it became clear there would be no clarity, he decided to move on and not keep asking for an explanation. Mishra said: “When someone does not want you, what can you do?” He was in an impressive run of form before the injury. In India’s five-match ODI series against New Zealand in 2016, Mishra took 15 wickets and was named Player of the Series. His best day came in the decisive fifth ODI in Visakhapatnam on October 29, when he took 5 for 18 as India won by 190 runs to clinch the series

But I didn’t get any answer; I never got a clear answer. That’s the only issue.” Why clear communication matters in selection decisions Mishra’s account is one side of a story, and it should be read that way, since Kohli has not been heard. Even so, the central complaint is a fair one that applies well beyond this case. Players can accept being dropped when they are told why, but they find it very hard to accept silence, especially when the last message they received was an assurance. A senior player who had just taken 15 wickets in a series deserved at least a clear answer on fitness, form or selection plans, and a short phone call would have cost very little. It is also fair to note that captains do not control selection alone, so the picture may be more complicated than a missed call. Indian cricket has often been criticised for how it handles veterans at the end of their careers. A simple system, with a named person responsible for telling players where they stand, would prevent stories like this one from surfacing years later. Mishra’s career deserved a proper full stop. item.title: Jurgen Klopp reveals he will support Barcelona over Real Madrid in El Clasico: ‘The better team’
item.description: Jurgen Klopp reveals he will support Barcelona over Real Madrid in El Clasico: ‘The better team’ It wasn’t long when Jurgen Klopp was considered a serious managerial candidate to replace Alvaro Arbeloa for the 2026/27 campaign. The German’s name was often sounded out throughout the presidential campaigns for the summer election. But Klopp did not want to leave Red Bull at the time, with Real Madrid ending up appointing Jose Mourinho. Three months into the new season, Klopp has taken up the role of the head coach for the German national team and it appears the former Liverpool manager has already taken sides. Klopp is ‘probably’ supporting Barcelona in El Clasico Heading into this weekend’s Clasico , Klopp was asked which team he will be rooting for. Klopp was linked with a move to Real Madrid in the summer. (Photo by Ricardo Moreira/Getty Images) In response, the German made no secret of his love for the fixture, admitting it is one he simply cannot ignore. “It’s a game I love to watch,” he told DAZN (h/t AS ). While he initially tried to remain impartial, Klopp ultimately conceded that his allegiance this weekend would lie with the side in the better form. “Today I’m supporting whoever is the better team. And as things stand, that team is probably Barcelona ,” he added. A Barcelona leaning rooted in the past Klopp will keep a close eye on the Clasico . (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images) The former Liverpool boss went on to explain that there was a time when he used to wholeheartedly support Barcelona over Real Madrid. “In the past, I was more of a Barcelona fan because I hated it when Pepe and the other defenders would rough up everything in their path back then. That was the only reason I supported Barcelona more ,” he explained. Given Klopp’s past of managing clubs like Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool, both of which are community driven, his liking for Barcelona is perhaps not that surprising. This weekend, though, the German will be caring less about a Barcelona win and more about how German players perform on the night, with Karim Adeyemi emerging as one of the players who could potentially make a difference as a late substitute.

item.description: Former India leg-spinner Amit Mishra believes an injury during the 2017 T20I against England in Bengaluru may have brought his international career to an early end. Mishra, who never played for India again after that match, claimed that then head coach Anil Kumble and captain Virat Kohli had assured him of a comeback once he regained full fitness. However, he alleged that Kohli stopped responding to his calls and messages after he recovered. Mishra made these claims during an episode of a podcast hosted by former India cricketer Aakash Chopra. He said the assurances from Kumble and Kohli did not translate into a return to the national team, with the match against England eventually becoming his final international appearance for India. "I got my leg injured during that time in Bangalore. And when I was leaving after getting injured, Anil Kumble was the coach. So I told Anil Bhai, I said, 'Anil Bhai...'. He said, 'Don't worry. As soon as you get fit, you will automatically come back,'" Mishra claimed during the podcast. He said he also spoke to Kohli, who had taken over as captain, and received a similar assurance about his place in the team. "Then, Virat Kohli became the captain after this. I also asked Virat Kohli, I said, 'Brother, what needs to be done?' He said, 'You don't worry. Get fully fit and comfortable, and you are there [in the team],'" he added. Mishra said that after recovering from the injury, he contacted Kohli to ask about his chances of returning to the Indian team. According to the leg-spinner, Kohli told him he would provide an update within seven to 10 days, but Mishra claimed he never heard back from the former India captain. — cricketaakash (@cricketaakash) "So, I went to him. I asked, 'Brother, what's the situation?' So he said, 'I will let you know in a week to ten days.' Then brother, one week passed, two weeks passed, three weeks passed, there was absolutely no update from him. I called him... so, he did not pick up the call. I messaged him, but there was no reply," Mishra said, accusing Kohli of failing to keep his promise. Mishra also said that several other players who had suffered more serious injuries and spent longer periods on the sidelines returned to the national team once they were fit. He felt he was not given the same opportunity and said he had never received an explanation for what happened. "I called again, he did not answer. I called twice more, still nothing... so I also let it go. Then I thought, 'Brother, what can we do?' When someone does not want you, what can you do? When players who got more severely injured than you, and were injured for much longer, made their comebacks... yet, I have never received any answer to this day."

Yet, despite being just 27 years old, the ninth-year star is familiar with standing directly in the spotlight as the centerpiece of a franchise. During his seven seasons with the Dallas Mavericks, Dončić won the Rookie of the Year, made five All-Star teams, claimed a scoring title, and led Dallas to an NBA Finals appearance. With a young star as their leader, the Mavericks looked set to keep building around Dončić. A surprise trade sent him to the Lakers. While Dončić and the Mavericks have moved on, an NBA insider added new context to the criticism that followed one of the NBA’s most shocking trades. item.title: Caleb Williams pokes fun at Richard Sherman for Bears ranking: ‘I see it all’
item.description: Credit: Prime Video Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams became a meme and the subject of unfair narratives when he draped a towel over his head while carted off the field in Week 2 of the NFL season. Williams suffered a hamstring injury, though he has since stated that “ every single ” report about the severity of his injury has been wrong. The 2024 No. 1 overall pick returned and declared himself “ inevitable ” last week, and it’s undeniable that Williams keeps tabs on what’s said about him and the Bears. On Thursday Night Football , the Bears beat the visiting New England Patriots, 30-24. Williams and Luther Burden III, the game’s leading receiver, joined the TNF Nightcap desk afterward, and Williams told Richard Sherman he’s keeping an eye on him. Caleb Williams getting MVP chants at the #TNFonPrime desk! https://t.co/3y2dqPJ0Ji — NFL on Prime Video (@NFLonPrime) October 23, 2026 “That time off, it added a little bit more to me,” Williams said. “And I’m gonna keep using it. I’m gonna keep bringing that energy, that fire in my eyes. I’m gonna release it to my teammates and, hopefully, to the fans. They feel my energy. Hopefully, we can get in your Top 5.” Sherman laughed through a gaping smile and slapped the desk. “I like that, Caleb!” he said. “He watches the podcast.” “I see it all,” Williams confirmed. On Wednesday’s episode of The Richard Sherman Podcast , Sherman and his co-host Mitch Eisenstein delivered their Top 5 lists. Eisenstein had the San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs, Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings, and Patriots. Sherman agreed with the first four of Eisenstein’s five, but he swapped the Patriots out for the Bears at No. 5. “No. 5, I do not agree with you, with the New England Patriots,” Sherman said on his podcast. “I got them losing Thursday night to the Chicago Bears and Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams. item.title: Barcelona director working behind the scenes on defender’s renewal after fighting display vs PSG
item.description: Barcelona director working behind the scenes on defender’s renewal after fighting display vs PSG The scoreline in the Barcelona vs PSG game could have looked a lot worse had it not been for some impressive performances from some of the youngter stars in the team. While Xavi Espart’s superb display has already been well documented, another player who deserves credit for his performance on the night is Gerard Martin. The young defender was heading into that game on the back of a knock picked up against Real Betis. Yet, he produced an excellent shift at the heart of the Barcelona backline. Gerard Martin’s performance vs PSG As reported by Mundo Deportivo , Martin was one of Barcelona’s more impressive performers in defence against PSG, despite an initial fear of injury. Gerard Martin will play a key role in the Clasico. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Although tests revealed no injury, caution was warranted, but Martin’s sheer determination ultimately earned him a place in the side. Despite not being at full fitness, the 24-year-old rose to the occasion against one of the most devastating attacks in world football. He finished the match with 14 recoveries, losing possession just once while winning every ground and aerial duel he contested. He also completed 58 passes at a 92% accuracy rate, won four rebounds and drew two fouls. Barring any late surprises, Martin will start again on Sunday in what will be his sixth Clasico in just three seasons, a list that already includes a standout showing against Rodrygo in the Copa del Rey final. Barcelona working on a renewal Barcelona want to secure Gerard Martin’s long-term future at the club. (Photo by Eric Alonso/Getty Images) The report adds that Martin’s steady rise has not gone unnoticed by the Barcelona hierarchy. Having surpassed the 100-game mark for the first team in little over two years, the defender has become one of the pillars of Flick’s side, forging a reliable partnership with Pau Cubarsi. As a result, Barcelona’s sporting director Deco is working to reward that progress with fresh terms. Martin’s current deal runs until 2028, but the club are pushing to extend it by a further two or three years, potentially until 2030 or 2031.

item.title: Real Madrid star speaks on Kylian Mbappé’s ‘dictator’ nickname
item.description: Real Madrid star speaks on Kylian Mbappé’s ‘dictator’ nickname Real Madrid star Thibaut Courtois has this week provided his take on the less-than-flattering nickname attributed to teammate Kylian Mbappé by the media. For those not aware, frontman Mbappé has long been christened the ‘dictator’ across the European press. This comes owing to widespread claims that the 27-year-old has a say in almost everything which goes on behind the scenes at club and international level alike, from signings to managerial appointments, contract details and beyond. Whether such claims are based in reality remains unclear, but Mbappé’s reputation appears all but set in stone. Speaking during an exchange with the media this week, the aforementioned Thibaut Courtois was therefore drawn on his teammate’s dictator nickname. And the Belgian, in his response, made clear that José Mourinho’s Real Madrid squad have long viewed the situation in a lighthearted fashion, explaining to DAZN: “Kylian Mbappé a dictator? We laugh about it in the dressing room all the time! We even sing the song… I think he finds it funny too.” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: ‘Can guard all positions’ – Gary Payton names his favourite defender in the NBA apart from his son
item.description: Photo by Brian Murphy/Icon Sportswire/Corbis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Gary Payton has named his son and Jrue Holiday as two of his favourite defenders in the modern NBA. Having made it to the All-Defensive First Team nine times, Payton is considered one of the greatest defenders in the NBA. His ability to guard multiple positions and strike fear in opponents with his trash talk were qualities that helped him become one of the pillars of the Seattle SuperSonics team in the 1990s. He continues to stay close to the game with media appearances and is also seen at NBA games as his son, Gary Payton II, plays for the Golden State Warriors. In his recent appearance on The Association, Payton was asked about his favourite defenders in the league and his answers were, unsurprisingly, his son and another legendary guard. Gary Payton names Jrue Holiday as one of his favourite NBA defenders, says he can guard one through five Gary Payton was not going to hide the bias of being a father when asked who his favourite NBA defender is when asked by Robin Lopez. However, his reasoning is why many would believe his take to be true. “I got to bring my son in here, I think he does a great job of what he does when he gets on the floor with the Golden State Warriors,” said Payton. Although he does not have the accolades to match his father’s resume, Gary Payton II is one of the best perimeter guards in the NBA. He can guard all positions and is also effective at scoring from beyond the arc. The 33-year-old was part of the Warriors team that won the championship in 2022. “I think he puts his foot into it and he locks down and he can guard all positions, I just love it as a guard, who can guard 94-feet,” Payton added. Holiday has six All-Defensive selections to his name, which shows how brilliant he has been since his arrival in the league. Alongside his elite defensive skill, Holiday has made his mark as a top decision-maker in the league. His leadership has helped him earn two championships, and he is currently leading a young Portland Trail Blazers side as they build a contender in the Western Conference. The team has players like Damian Lillard, Ja Morant and Deni Avdija, but what Holiday brings is his elite championship experience, which young players need to be surrounded by in their initial years. item.title: Jaylen Brown emoji breathes new life into beef narrative with Jayson Tatum
item.description: Rumors of a supposed beef between star Boston Celtics forward Jayson Tatum and now- Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown are nothing new under the sun. But a recent documentary video release by Tatum and social media comment on it by Brown have breathed new life into this tired narrative. In that video, Tatum talks about the Georgia native being dealt to the Philadelphia 76ers, and his surprise at the move when he learned Brown was being dealt to a division rival. "(Celtics assistant coach God Shammgod, Jr.) handed me a towel," said Tatum in said video. "He was like, 'Yo, put this over your face. Don't react. They just traded him.' I'm like, 'Oh, shit.' I'm like, 'Where?' He said, 'Philly.' I said, 'You traded him down the street?' So I was just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world." Brown, evidently, took issue with at least some of this take, commenting on social media with an emoji of a hat to signify (assumedly) he was calling 'cap' on those words – slang for untrue for the olds among us. This stands in contrasts to the considerable lengths that Tatum has gone since the trade went down to make it clear he bears no ill will toward his former teammate, even going as far as to praise his tenure with Boston and the impact it had on his own career. Something else, it appears, is simmering on the other side of this well-worn narrative. Perhaps, however, this time it actually has teeth. item.title: NBA Scout Predicts Joel Embiid Will ‘Railroad’ Philadelphia 76ers Season For a Very Petty Reason
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While the Philadelphia 76ers have been impressive in their first two games of the new season, an NBA scout firmly believes it is only a matter of time before Joel Embiid puts his personal success ahead of his team’s. After winning the offseason by trading for Jaylen Brown and signing NBA icon LeBron James, the 76ers are the most fascinating story in the league to begin the 2026-27 campaign. The two All-Stars were added to a roster that already included Embiid and a top-10 scoring talent in Tyrese Maxey. On paper, they could be fantastic. If their stars are willing to sacrifice their numbers at the altar of success. Well, so far so good, because Philadelphia owns a 2-0 record to begin the campaign after very nice wins over the defending champion New York Knicks and the Cleveland Cavaliers . NBA scout on Joel Embiid: ‘He’s going to get pissed. He’s going to stop playing defense’ Furthermore, Embiid’s play on both sides of the floor has been encouraging, since he is the star who will probably need to sacrifice the most on offense so the 76ers can be a legitimate title contender. However, in a new report from ESPN’s Tim MacMahon, a rival scout told the NBA insider he is not sold on the idea that Embiid will make big sacrifices and expects him to undercut their title hopes. “ I think it’s going to be a problem, and that could railroad them . I just don’t buy it right now. He’s going to want the ball more. He’s going to get pissed. He’s going to stop playing defense. He’s going to stop running.” – NBA scout The seven-time All-Star slimmed down in the offseason in the hopes that it would allow him to be a difference-maker on defense and keep him healthy. Embiid’s defense was a problem during last year’s playoffs, and the Knicks targeted him often. The one-time MVP has not played in more than 60 games since the 2022-23 season. item.title: Fantasy Football Injury Impact: Emeka Egbuka Is Ruled OUT For Week 7, Opening The Door For Ted Hurst III
item.description: Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (2) runs after a catch for a touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have ruled out their top wide receiver, Emeka Egbuka, for Week 7. He was dealing with a concussion and a foot injury. Because he has a concussion, we don't really know much about the foot injury, as he has not been able to practice. This was always the likely outcome once he was put in the league's concussion protocol on Monday, which he was not able to clear. Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Panthers. Via @gregauman pic.twitter.com/sXMy5Y4BNb - RotoWire Fantasy Football (@RotoWireNFL) October 23, 2026 Fantasy Impact WR Emeka Egbuka, Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is a tough break for Egbuka and a tough loss for fantasy football owners. He stepped up with Jalon Daniels under center, catching seven of 16 targets for 48 yards and a touchdown last week, and finding the end zone in back-to-back weeks. His numbers haven't been incredible, but he did more than expected with an undrafted rookie backup quarterback. It would have been nice to have him in our lineups this week with Baker Mayfield back on the field. Egbuka's focus will now turn to getting back on the field in Week 8. The concussion seems to be the bigger issue than the foot injury. WR Ted Hurst III, Tampa Bay Buccaneers Hurst is the next man up and should be picked up immediately if he's sitting on the waiver wire. He will likely see his offensive snaps jump to about 80%, and he is coming off a week in which he saw six targets, catching three of them for 40 yards. We love the opportunity, but he should still be considered a risky flex option. He's still a rookie third-round pick whose career-high in receiving is 40 yards. That doesn't mean that he can't have a breakout game, but it's also not safe to bank on a career day. You can start him in your flex; just manage your expectations and hope he reaches his upside. WR Chris Godwin, Tampa Bay Buccaneers Godwin has had a decent floor this season, but very little upside. He hasn't scored a touchdown and has maxed out at 46 yards. There is a chance that his ceiling will rise with Egbuka ruled out. However, there is also a chance that the 30-year-old receiver just doesn't have that much left in the tank. He should see a boost in PPR leagues, but we still don't see him having much upside otherwise. item.title: Colts announce bad news on Tyler Warren, Sauce Gardner for Week 7
item.description: Colts announce bad news on Tyler Warren, Sauce Gardner for Week 7 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts are 2-4 on the year and just lost to the Tennessee Titans in Week 6. After that brutal loss, the Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard. A lot of focus is now on the Colts, with plenty of teams interested in the potential trade targets they could acquire from Indianapolis. But the Colts are willing to give the Colts and Shane Steichen a chance this season. Unfortunately, it just got very hard for Week 7. ESPN's Adam Schefter reports that the Colts announced that both tight end Tyler Warren and cornerback Sauce Gardner are going to miss the team's Week 7 matchup. It's two brutal blows for very important players for a team that needs all the help they can get. Colts get bad news as Tyler Warren and Sauce Gardner are ruled out for Week 7 "Colts HC Shane Steichen ruled out CB Sauce Gardner (calf) and TE Tyler Warren (groin) for Sunday's game vs. the Vikings ," Schefter reports. This is a huge piece of news for the Colts, as they're now down two of their most important players for their Week 7 matchup against the undefeated Minnesota Vikings. The Vikings are an elite defense, so losing such a good receiver in Warren is a tough blow for Indianapolis' offense this week. MORE : Why Colts are likely sellers after firing Chris Ballard before NFL trade deadline But the really big loss is Gardner, especially considering who he would've been covering on the Vikings. Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison are two elite receivers, and they might be in store for a huge day against the Colts with Gardner out. While neither player is likely to miss a lot more time, both players are missing Week 7, which has become an important game for a Colts team on the verge of some major changes this season. Daniel Jones and the Colts are facing quite the uphill battle in Week 7 against the Vikings, and that was even before the Warren and Gardner injury updates were revealed. item.title: North Florida Christian retiring local legend Ernie Sims jersey
item.description: The number 34 will never be worn again on the famed grass of North Florida Christian's football field. Ernie Sims , one of the best players in program history and former No. 1 overall recruit in the nation in 2003, will have his jersey retired at halftime of the Eagles' home game against Marianna . Sims won four state championships with NFC before embarking on a three-year career with Florida State and eight years in the NFL. He is heralded as one of the Seminoles' best linebackers, earning All-American honors. Sims recorded 200 tackles, including 21.0 for loss with 7.0 sacks, three forced fumbles, two interceptions, one fumble recovery, and one blocked kick. He won a pair of ACC titles with the program before he was the No. 9 overall pick in the 2006 NFL Draft, selected by the Detroit Lions. Over his eight-year NFL career, Sims accumulated 623 total tackles, with 26.0 tackles for loss and 5.5 sacks, 14 quarterback hurries, six forced fumbles, three fumble recoveries, and one interception, spending time with the Lions, Philadelphia Eagles, Indianapolis Colts, and Dallas Cowboys. Sims currently serves as the linebackers coach for FSU . Despite some struggles from the Seminoles, Sims's linebacker unit is one of the best on the team, led by Chris Jones. NFC is 2-6 and hosts Marianna (3-4) at 7 p.m., looking for a shock win on a special night. Liam Rooney covers Florida State athletics for the Tallahassee Democrat. item.title: Bills’ 7-round 2027 NFL Draft according to PFF mock draft simulator during bye week
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Bills’ 7-round 2027 NFL Draft according to PFF mock draft simulator during bye week appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Buffalo Bills head to their bye week at 4-1, riding high after navigating a tough part of their schedule. While the record is good, there are some issues the team is dealing with on both sides of the ball. The NFL trade deadline may help with that , but after that, they’ll be looking at the 2027 NFL Draft for reinforcements. So, we asked the PFF 2027 NFL Mock Draft simulator what the Bills would do in April, and here’s what it came back with. Round 1, Pick 27: S Ty Benefield, LSU It’s no secret that the Bills’ secondary is the weakness of the team right now. Cole Bishop and Christian Benford are finally starting to play better, and Davison Igbinosun is showing promise, but the rest of the group is a mess. Maxwell Hairston and Damar Hamlin are not starting-caliber players, and neither is Chauncey Gardner-Johnson (when he’s not spitting on people). item.title: Atlanta Falcons Quietly Swap Photo After Profile Image Sparks Uproar with Nazi Comparisons
item.description: Credit: Perry Knotts/Getty; Atlanta Falcons/X NEED TO KNOW The team posted a throwback-inspired profile image before replacing it with a helmet graphic Social media users compared the design’s red background and stripes to Nazi Germany imagery A logo historian said the Falcons likely had no ill intent during their throwback weekend promotion The Atlanta Falcons are under fire after showcasing a profile picture that’s drawn comparisons to imagery of Nazi Germany. On Wednesday, Oct. 21, the NFL team posted the image on X, a throwback to the Falcons’ 1966 design centered on a red background with white, black and gold stripes. “New PFP [profile picture],” the Falcons captioned the post. The image drew mixed reactions on social media, with some comparing the graphic to the World War II German eagle logo. “Who thought this was a good idea?” asked one X user, while another called out, “This looks like the symbol for a flag in a dystopian cyberpunk Video game where the Nazis won WW2.” New PFP 👀 pic.twitter.com/gBXWISJav4 — Atlanta Falcons (@AtlantaFalcons) October 21, 2026 Another said , “The amount of people who had to approve this is staggering and yet here we are.” Others called for the team to apologize, with one user stating : “Please admin don’t be soft and delete this or issue an apology.” Atlanta Falcons logo Credit: Atlanta Falcons/X Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! The controversial image was replaced. As of Friday, Oct. 23, a graphic of a red helmet currently occupies the profile picture slot. The organization has not publicly addressed the backlash as of Friday. Sports logo historian Chris Creamer told NBC News he believes the Falcons had “no ill intent” with the image and he “can’t imagine in a million years” that the team did it purposefully. The team also announced that it is unveiling a new “throwback” uniform. Described as a “modern interpretation of this historic fifty-year-old design,” the Falcons’ black Nike jersey will boast “a bold white name and number font trimmed in red, and the original Falcon crest on both sleeves” and will be “paired with white pants and socks — both highlighted by a distinctive bold red and black stripe pattern,” according to the team’s official website . The Falcons host the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, Oct. 25. Read the original article on People

item.title: Detroit Lions unveil plan for Brian Branch in return to action
item.description: The Detroit Lions are ready to rip the Band-Aid off with Cade Mays , and it appears as if they'll take the same approach with Brian Branch. Lions coach Dan Campbell said Friday, Oct. 23, the Lions are "going to let [Branch] go" in his season debut Sunday, Oct. 25, against the Green Bay Packers . Branch, a Pro Bowl player in 2024 and one of the most versatile safeties in football, has not played a game in more than 10 months since tearing his Achilles tendon in a win over the Dallas Cowboys last Dec. 4. He returned to practice Oct. 7. "Yeah, we got a pretty good idea with him," Campbell said. "We're going to let him go here and we'll be smart, but he's ready to play. ” Campbell indicated in a radio interview this week that he planned to start Mays at center in his first action of the season this week. WORDS HURT? Dan Campbell trying to keep TE Sam LaPorta comments from becoming distraction Mays broke his right wrist in training camp, returned to practice the same day as Branch and is set to come off injured reserve this week. Previously, Campbell had debated the idea of rotating Mays and his replacement, Juice Scruggs, at center. "I think right now the plan − Juice has done a hell of a job for us and I’ve mentioned this before, I’m going to continue to say it, that was – thank goodness we got Juice, man," Campbell said in an interview on 97.1 The Ticket (WXYT-FM). "He’s been outstanding for us. "That being said, we really worked the heck out of Cade yesterday, he got some quality reps and we would like to give him a go here and not make that move. And then obviously Juice is starting off swinging between center and guard, as needed at center and some guard. But yeah, we’d like to just rip this Band-Aid off of Cade. I thought he had some good work yesterday. I thought he looked pretty good." Scruggs is the second-highest graded center in the NFL, according to Pro Football Focus. Campbell explained his reasoning for wanting to get Mays back in the lineup Friday. "Well, look, we went and got Cade for a reason and there’s things we know that he brings to us mentally and physically, and he’s a little different player than Juice and Juice has done a really good job," Campbell said. "But this gets us starting to trend to who are our best five. And maybe it is this lineup here, but Juice will certainly be involved in all that as we move forward." item.title: Joaquin Seys: Man United target makes major admission about his future
item.description: Joaquin Seys: Man United target makes major admission about his future Manchester United’s pursuit of Luke Shaw’s heir has seen them linked with several left-backs from across the continent. The Red Devils are drawing up succession plans for the English full-back, whose contract expires at the end of this season. Shaw was outstanding last campaign, but is already on the wrong side of 30 and has displayed signs of regression this season. The 31-year-old started every game in the Premier League last campaign, a feat he managed for the first time in his career. However, Shaw has appeared in just five of United’s 11 games in all competitions this campaign. The Red Devils are already short of options for the position, with Patrick Dorgu injured and Harry Amass lacking top-flight experience. The situation has seen Noussair Mazraoui, Diogo Dalot and even Ayden Heaven operate in the role in Shaw’s absence. The English giants are expected to address the situation at the turn of the year, and one of the candidates reportedly on their wish list is Club Brugge star Joaquin Seys. United could sign a new left-back in January United’s poor start to the season could prompt INEOS to invest heavily in the squad at the turn of the year. The Red Devils wanted to sign a new left-back this summer, but failed to get any of their targets after investing over £150 million in the midfield. That decision has come back to haunt the club, which is now 13th in the Premier League table after seven games, with just one win to its name. The English giants are expected to make amends in the winter transfer window, and recent reports suggest they are keeping Seys under close watch. The Belgian speedster has been in fine form this season, scoring one goal and registering four assists in 13 appearances in all competitions. J. Seys The 21-year-old’s performances make him a promising long-term successor for Shaw at the Theatre of Dreams, further adding to speculation regarding a possible move. Seys has now provided a key update on his future. Seys happy at Club Brugge for now Speaking to Voetbal Nieuws , Seys insisted that he remains fully focused on giving his best with Club Brugge. When asked about the rumoured interest from top clubs in Europe, Seys responded: “To be honest, I haven’t really given it much thought yet.” The Belgian insisted that he remains settled with Club Brugge, but appeared to leave the door open for a future transfer away from the club. He continued: “This is the club I love, so it’s brilliant that I’ve already been able to play so many matches here.” “This is the club closest to my heart, so I’d give my all for them. I’m focusing entirely on Club Brugge right now, and after that we’ll see what happens.” Final Thoughts Seys fits the profile of talented young footballers that United have targeted in recent times. While the Belgian could be a fantastic addition to the squad, the only concern regarding the move would be his lack of Premier League experience. Featu

item.title: Liverpool sent scouts to watch 21-year-old midfielder in the Champions League
item.description: Liverpool sent scouts to watch 21-year-old midfielder in the Champions League Liverpool scouts track Aleksey Batrakov after Galatasaray Champions League impact Liverpool’s recruitment operation appears to be doing what it often does best, gathering information early, quietly and with purpose. According to TeamTalk , club scouts were present to watch Galatasaray attacker Aleksey Batrakov in Champions League action this week, where the 21-year-old found the net in a 4-2 win away at Lille. Arsenal were also reportedly represented, while Chelsea, Manchester City and Manchester United are all credited with interest in the young playmaker. For Liverpool, this looks like another example of market awareness around a player whose trajectory is moving quickly in the right direction. Batrakov only joined Galatasaray from Lokomotiv Moscow in the summer, yet his profile is already growing. The report states that his contract contains a £50m release clause, a figure that would naturally sharpen attention if his form continues on the European stage. It is also an important detail that his move to Turkiye has changed the practical landscape around any future transfer, after previous UK government sanctions had blocked the possibility of a direct switch from Russia. Batrakov emerging as a Liverpool transfer option The timing of this development is notable. Liverpool are assessing how their attacking midfield and forward support options should evolve under Andoni Iraola, and Batrakov’s skill set appears to align with many of the principles associated with the head coach. He is described in the original reporting as a technically gifted attacking player with strong decision-making, game intelligence and a high-level work rate. Photo: IMAGO Those qualities matter. Iraola’s teams demand intensity, sharp reactions, tactical discipline and the ability to make good choices at speed. Batrakov’s growing reputation suggests he may be capable of fitting into that framework, especially if Liverpool are looking at players who can operate between the lines, press aggressively and contribute goals. Galatasaray rise puts £50m release clause under spotlight What will further encourage observers is the calibre of the occasions in which Batrakov is producing. He has now scored in consecutive Champions League matches, following up his goal against Barcelona with another in France. That tends to accelerate conversations inside elite clubs, particularly when recruitment staff have the chance to watch a player live rather than rely solely on data and video work. At 21, he sits in an age bracket Liverpool have repeatedly valued, young enough to develop, experienced enough to handle major environments, and already attracting broad Premier League attention. Galatasaray may have moved decisively to secure him, but the sense from this report is that interest around him is only building. item.title: Hope College women's basketball reloads 2026-27 roster after run to Sweet 16
item.description: The Hope College women's basketball team has released its roster for the 2026-27 season and it will be a reloading season for the Flying Dutch. Hope was 26-4 last year, winning the MIAA Tournament and reaching the Sweet 16 of the NCAA Division III Tournament. Hope will return starters Terin Maynard (guard), Leah Richards (center), Anna Richards (guard) and Maddie Petroelje (guard/forward) as well as backup point guard/sixth woman Josie DeSmit. The only starter who graduated was Sydney Vis. More: Hope women's basketball falls in NCAA sectional as last-second shot misses mark That leaves one starting spot that could go a number of directions. If the Flying Dutch want to go with a smaller lineup, senior Chloe Brunsberg would be the likely choice. If they want to go big, Katie Blazei might be the fifth starter. Freshmen on the team include Sophia Prins (Byron Center, South Christian), Lizzie Wolthuis (Byron Center, South Christian), Olivia Jones (Pendleton, Ind.) and Payton Wallin (Minooka Ill.). Seniors are Brunsberg, Meynard, guard Emma Yakey and center Grayson Guy. Juniors include the Richards sisters, Blazei and Petroelje. Sophomores are DeSmit, guard Bayli Stewart, guard Gillian Sorrelle and forward Sydney Bode. The Flying Dutch tip off the season at 5:30 p.m. Nov. 6, when they host Wisconsin-Platteville at DeVos Fieldhouse in the Michele Schoon Tournament. item.title: ‘We want to have more and be more’ – Crystal Palace want to improve says Potter
item.description: ‘We want to have more and be more’ – Crystal Palace want to improve says Potter Crystal Palace head coach Jo Potter says that her side want to keep improving off the back of their solid start to life back in the Barclays Women’s Super League. The Eagles have taken six points from their six games so far and occupy 11th place in the league table. Reflecting on what Crystal Palace have achieved so far, head coach Potter said that her side have lacked consistency at times and that they are wanting to improve further. “It has been a little bit up and down,” Potter said when speaking to the media ahead of this weekend’s fixture against Chelsea. “We need a little bit more consistency in all of our areas which comes with being a new team [to the league] and trying to find your feet in the WSL. “We are working to a way and we are always trying to improve. We are not taking anything for granted, but we want to improve, we want to be better. We are not settling and being happy with where we are at, we want to have more and be more. “We are going to continue with that and keep pushing because it’s a long old season and there are still plenty more games to go.” Latest opponents Chelsea are unbeaten so far this season and Potter sees a side that are now getting back to their best after a poor campaign in 2025/2026. She said “It’s always tough when you have a transition period and what it looks like in terms of the signings that they’ve made and some of the outgoings that left the building. “What you always see with Chelsea is that they’re an efficient team, they have a clear identity, a clear way of playing and some real world-class players. They’re always going to be a tough team to play against. You’ve just got to try and limit those moments and opportunities. “They’re on a real good run of form at the moment and look really dangerous.” Chelsea midfielder Lexi Potter could face her former club this weekend. The midfielder previously enjoyed a successful loan spell with Crystal Palace. Eagles boss Potter said that Crystal Palace played a significant part in the youngster’s development. She said “The Palace fans love her. One thing about this club is that the fans adore their players; they were chanting for her in the cup game last season and she wasn’t even on the pitch. “I think it [the loan spell] was definitely integral in Lexi’s journey, her development and where she is now; getting exposure to WSL minutes super-early in her career. I think it was huge for her and it has put her in a much better place kicking on at Chelsea.” Crystal Palace’s Barclays Women’s Super League fixture against Chelsea kicks-off at 12pm on Sunday afternoon.

We have acquired: 🏒 F Dawson Mercer 🏒 F Alexander Command 🏒 G Nico Daws 🏒 F Nick Bjugstad 🔢 and two draft picks pic.twitter.com/vAN00bP0dO — Winnipeg Jets (@NHLJets) October 23, 2026 Connor Hellebuyck Trade Happens as His Team Suspension Ends As Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman reported last week , Hellebuyck was set to have his team suspension from the Winnipeg Jets end today. Given that a reconciliation between team and player was unlikely, it would have been a bad idea to welcome Hellebuyck back into the Winnipeg dressing room. Thus, a Connor Hellebuyck trade needed to be facilitated quickly. It has been a tough go as of late for the Jets after a good start, but they are getting solid goaltending from Stuart Skinner , which makes the Hellebuyck trade a bit easier to take. Devils GM Sunny Mehta Makes His First Bold Blockbuster Trade The Devils were not messing around here, as they gave up a lot in order to get Hellebuyck to bolster their goaltending, which has been middling so far. Dawson Mercer, 24 years old, is a solid middle-six player who has had decent seasons up to this point. He had 20 goals and 22 assists for 42 points in 82 games last season. This season so far, he has had four assists in 10 games. Mercer was New Jersey’s first-round pick (18th overall) in 2020. He is a versatile forward who is smart and durable and can play in many situations, including physical situations, as well as on the penalty kill. A big piece of this trade has to be Alexander Command, who was the 12th overall pick in 2026 for the Devils. He was ranked 21st in Last Word on Hockey’s draft rankings and was praised for his explosive speed and high-end compete level. The 18-year-old is projected to be a top-six to top-nine forward, but young prospects will always have the potential to be something more. Apr 13, 2026; Las Vegas, Nevada, USA; Vegas Golden Knights right wing Pavel Dorofeyev (16) scores a goal against Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck (37) during the third period at T-Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Stephen R. Sylvanie-Imagn Images Nico Daws is the goaltender the Jets picked up in this trade and could be the backup now behind Skinner. Daws is a 25-year-old who has played four games for the Devils this season, posting a 2-2-0 record with a 2.78 goals-against average and an .874 save percentage. He was New Jersey’s third-round pick (84th overall) in the 2020 NHL Draft and has compiled a 26-26-1 record in 59 career NHL games and posted a shutout, a 2.94 goals-against average and an .897 save percentage. Nick Bjugstad is a veteran centre who is recovering from surgery at the moment . The 34-year-old recorded nine points in 61 games last season for the St. Louis Blues and New Jersey Devils. A decent depth piece for the Jets to acquire. The Jets still have roughly $8 million in cap space after this transaction, according to PuckPedia . Does the Connor Hellebuyck Trade Improve the Devils’ Outlook? Hellebuyck will likely improve the Devils’ goaltending, but to say it will certainly make them a contender is jumping the gun. They are giving up prime assets for an aging goaltender who has not seen game action in over six months. However, the price may have depreciated over time, and GM Sunny Mehta capitalized on the opportunity, not giving up any future first-round picks in the process. Time will tell, but this may have been a smart move. The Last Word Finally, the Hellebuyck saga in Winnipeg has come to an end. With that drama over, the Jets can now focus on the present, making sure they bounce back from last season. They may need goaltending help in the future, but Skinner could hold the fort for a while. For the Devils, the Connor Hellebuyck trade is a high-risk, potentially high-reward trade for them, as they needed an upgrade in goaltending, and Mehta got it done. The Devils could be going all-in this season, but time will tell what their direction holds after the Connor Hellebuyck trade. item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.content:encoded: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. item.content:encoded: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
